page: Amazon Web Services c6in.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 54 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for AVX-512 vector processing and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI instruction sets. The host is provisioned with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The server profile does not include bundled local storage, requiring persistent workloads to utilize remote network-attached volumes. Networking provides a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps, while no discrete GPU hardware is present. Benchmark results indicate consistent average performance across compute and memory workloads, scoring 1,501.0 in Geekbench single-core, 5,599.0 in multi-core, and 11,053.75 in PassMark CPU tests. The memory subsystem records 412.8 GB/sec for small-block cached reads and 48.61 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads. Application benchmarks demonstrate 7.93 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.28 GB/sec in static web throughput. Relative weaknesses appear in bzip3 decompression and medium-size model prompt processing, where 7B LLM inference scores 15.51 tokens per second.

Regarding qualitative cost efficiency, the c6in.2xlarge provides high network throughput and dedicated CPU allocation without the infrastructure overhead of local NVMe storage arrays. The 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio restricts its utility for memory-heavy databases or large parameter artificial intelligence models. As a result, the instance is most appropriate for compute-bound and network-bound applications, such as distributed compilation pipelines, static web serving, network appliances, and stateless containerized services.
description: Amazon Web Services c6in.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance utilizing the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. It delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, paired with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory to maintain a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance includes no bundled local storage and operates with a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Compute performance falls squarely within the median range across standard industry benchmarks, featuring a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,599.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 11,053.75. Memory bandwidth reaches 48.61 GB/sec on large reads, though performance decreases during medium LLM inference tasks. Without local disk capacity or GPU acceleration, this configuration is technically aligned with network-intensive microservices, web serving clusters, and software compilation tasks.
